verdict.rationale: Honeycomb's core alerting mechanisms (Triggers, SLO burn alerts) explicitly require hand-configured thresholds, not automated anomaly detection. However, BubbleUp (docs-28) and the MCP agent integration explicitly describe 'identifying performance outliers' (docs-10/20/26) during investigation, showing some threshold-free outlier surfacing, but this is investigative/on-demand rather than a proactive alerting feature that replaces threshold-based rules. Missing for 10: evidence of an automated, always-on anomaly-detection alert that fires without any configured threshold, and independent confirmation that BubbleUp/MCP outlier detection functions as a genuine alerting substitute rather than a manual investigation aid.
